To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hybrid scheme has the best availability, and is the best choice of the four algorithms.

a hybrid scheme that uses static voting for the primary copies and dynamic voting for the secondary copies has the best file availability among voting, static voting, dynamic voting and dynamic voting with ordered copies.

a hybrid voting algorithm combining static and dynamic voting has the most availability for all repair/failure ratios, and the hybrid algorithm has a lower average message overhead than dynamic voting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hybrid scheme that combines static voting and dynamic voting with a linear ordering of copies.
the design, analysis, and evaluation of the availability of replicated data.

the design of a new voting scheme that combines the advantages of static voting and dynamic voting with a linearly ordered copies, and that is superior to both static voting and dynamic with linearly ordered copy in terms of availability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid voting protocol is superior to the other voting protocols for all reasonable values of the repair/failure ratio.
the hybrid scheme is a very good algorithm for a system with a high repair/failure ratio and a low number of copies.
dynamic voting with linear ordering is the best replica control protocol in the presence of a high repair rate and a low failure rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hybrid scheme has a higher availability than voting for all repair/failure ratios, has a higher availability that dynamic voting for repair/failure ratios of.1 or greater, and has a higher availability with linearly ordered dynamic voting for all reasonable repair failure ratios.
the proposed algorithm is the best algorithm in terms of availability and the number of replicas needed.

the hybrid scheme is the most efficient of the four schemes for most repair/failure ratios and the dynamic voting with linear ordered copies scheme is the least efficient of these four schemes for most values of the repair/failure ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid voting algorithm is the most efficient algorithm for ensuring high availability in a replicated file system.
a hybrid scheme that integrates static voting and dynamic voting with replication is the most available of the four algorithms tested.
a hybrid scheme can be more efficient than either static voting or dynamic voting alone.
